questions.q: What is the null hypothesis of the ADF test?
options: The series has a unit root (non-stationary)
why: That is the KPSS null.
Correct.
ADF does not test for trend that way.
White noise is a special stationary case.

questions.q: ADF p-value is 0.002. At alpha = 0.05 you conclude...
options: Reject the unit root: the series looks stationary
why: Correct.
That would be a large p-value.
A small p-value is a valid result.
The test does not detect seasonality.

questions.q: acf(x, nlags=24) returns how many values?
questions.why: It returns lags 0 to 24, which is 25 values. Lag 0 is always 1.

questions.q: Scenario: ADF on a series with a strong upward trend gives p = 0.97. After one difference p = 0.0001. What is d in ARIMA(p, d, q)?
questions.why: One difference made the series stationary, so d = 1.

questions.q: Scenario: your ACF plot of a trending series decays slowly and shows no clear season. What do you do first?
options: Difference the series (or remove the trend with STL) and look at the ACF again
why: A slow decay is a trend symptom.
Correct: the trend hides the seasonal peaks.
No need to delete data.
More lags will not remove the trend.
